title: [RFC]: Token-level streaming text input for TTS: commitment policy, capacity-aware segmentation, and speech-state inheritance
body:
### Motivation.

vLLM-Omni TTS today accepts either a complete prompt or, on the omni path, chunked tokens forwarded from an upstream stage. Neither path asks the question that streaming text actually forces: *is this text safe to speak yet?* #1766 has been open since March asking for streaming input on Qwen3-TTS, and it has no design behind it.

The reason the question is hard is that audio has no undo. Text on a screen can be silently rewritten; a spoken syllable cannot be recalled. If the buffer holds `2026` and the next token is `年`, it reads "twenty twenty-six"; if the next token is `元`, it reads "two thousand and twenty-six yuan". Speak before that token arrives and the output is wrong with no recovery. Chunk-forwarding with no readability gate does exactly that.

X2Streaming-TTS (arXiv [2608.18661](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18661), MIT-licensed, X Square Robot) publishes a recipe for this with measured results. Two things make it worth an RFC here rather than a link in a comment:

1. **The algorithms are engine-agnostic; their implementation is not.** Their code is a policy layer over a TensorRT engine ([X2Streaming-TTS](https://github.com/X-Square-Robot/X2Streaming-TTS) on top of [Qwen3TTS-Streaming](https://github.com/X-Square-Robot/Qwen3TTS-Streaming)). What transfers to vLLM-Omni is the decision logic, not the kernels.
2. **Roughly half the state machinery already exists in tree**, listed per-mechanism below. This is closer to connecting existing pieces than to a from-scratch feature.

The paper's key observation is worth stating because the whole design rests on it: text carries information densely, speech spends it slowly. Define the expansion ratio `ρ_k = A_k / n_k`, the number of autoregressive acoustic decoding steps per text token. Measured `ρ` is well above 1, so playback progress is naturally slower than text arrival. That is why zero-lookahead works at all: while the model speaks the tokens it already has, the next tokens arrive on their own. Methods that need lookahead borrow future tokens and stall the upstream LLM; this borrows time that speaking already costs.

### Proposed Change.

Three mechanisms, each mapped to what exists and what is missing. The ablation in the paper reports all three are needed: without commitment the system is forced to cut at linguistically wrong points and hallucinates on hard text; without inheritance, seams show audible timbre and prosody jumps.

#### Mechanism 1: zero-lookahead commitment

Split the buffered text into a **stable prefix** (no legal continuation can change its reading) and a **pending tail** (numbers, units, symbols, abbreviations still open). Re-split on every arriving token. Two invariants: normalization is atomic (resolve `2026元` to its spoken form as a unit, never hand the acoustic model a half-normalized string), and release is final (released text is never revised, emitted audio is never cut).

This is a deterministic safety check, not a probabilistic guess: if any legal continuation could change the reading, do not release.

| | Status |
|---|---|
| Exists | nothing model-agnostic. Text frontends are per-model: `glm_tts/text_frontend.py`, `indextts2/text_processing_v2_5.py`, `ming_flash_omni/text_processing.py` |
| Missing | the commitment policy itself, and a shared home for it |

Proposed home: a model-agnostic module under `vllm_omni/model_executor/stage_input_processors/`, consumed by the TTS stage-0 input processor. It must not live inside a model directory, or the second model to need it will copy it.

#### Mechanism 2: capacity-adaptive, punctuation-aware segmentation

Estimate `ρ` from the *realized* decode steps and text tokens of the segment that just finished. Divide remaining decoder capacity by that estimate to get how many text tokens the next segment can hold. Rank punctuation by strength (sentence-final, clause-level, weaker pauses); as the budget drains, accept progressively weaker punctuation as a cut point, and hard-cut only when the ceiling is reached. Freeze a segment's budget and thresholds when it opens so the rule does not shift mid-segment.

| | Status |
|---|---|
| Exists | `chunk_size_utils.parse_chunk_ramp` and `codec_chunk_ramp` in `qwen3_tts_code2wav.py` (L17, L158, L667). This is a **static** ramp read from `extra_cfg` |
| Missing | measuring `ρ` and feeding it back; punctuation ranking; the budget freeze |

The change is to make the existing ramp measured rather than declared. Related: #4913 (streaming chunk gap) and #5889 (short Chinese request reaching stage-0 `max_tokens` and emitting trailing noise) are both symptoms of segmentation that does not know its own budget.

The paper proves a bound on fragmentation: segment count is at most `(1/α₁)·m* + 1` where `m*` is the theoretical minimum and `α₁ = 0.7`, so `10/7 ≈ 1.43x`. That matters for review: it means the policy cannot silently degenerate into over-segmentation.

#### Mechanism 3: causal speech-state inheritance

Two independent paths across a segment boundary. Carry the **full** Code2Wav decoder state so the next segment warm-starts instead of restarting from silence. Carry only a **fixed** number of Talker alignment states as recent history: the paper fixes `H = 4` for all runs, so inheritance cost is constant and does not grow with stream length.

| | Status |
|---|---|
| Exists | `Qwen3TTSCode2Wav._decoder_state_cache`, keyed by `req_id` (`qwen3_tts_code2wav.py:110`), already carries decoder state per request |
| Missing | inheriting it across *segment* boundaries inside one stream, and any bounded Talker-side history |

The Code2Wav half is close. The Talker half is new. This is the same class of problem we already hit on Higgs v3, where `async_chunk` needed a stateful Code2Wav to avoid seam artifacts.

#### Reported results

From the paper, for calibration. We have not reproduced any of these.

| Property | X2Streaming-TTS | Best compared baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Ambiguity diagnostic CER | 2.00% | 6.65% (CosyVoice 3-S) |
| Ambiguity full-read rate | 73.3% | 40.0% |
| Hard-cut share / capacity utilization | 0.54% / 76.93% | fixed window 87.13% / 92.48%; punctuation only 0% / 11.77% |
| Boundary discontinuity (PBD) | 0.1092 [0.1000, 0.1192] | 0.1915 [0.1794, 0.2041] (FireRedTTS-2) |
| Long-range speaker self-similarity | 0.9511 [0.9454, 0.9565] | 0.5205 [0.4165, 0.6178] (FireRedTTS-2) |

The segmentation row is the interesting one: the two naive policies each win exactly one column and lose the other badly. The two continuity rows are also worth reading together, since the nearest competitor on seam smoothness has the worst long-range timbre stability. Smooth seams and stable speaker identity are separate properties.

**On the latency numbers.** The paper reports client-side first-audio median of 15.8 ms single-request, 118.6 ms at 64-way, 260.8 ms at 128-way on one RTX 5090. That is a deployed BF16 TensorRT engine with fixed complete requests, a fixed speaker, and prefix cache hits. It is not comparable to a vLLM-Omni number and should not be quoted as a target. What we should adopt is the measurement methodology (client-observed first audio chunk, median plus P99, swept over concurrency), which we do not currently report per-concurrency for TTS at all.

#### Open questions

1. **Scope of mechanism 1.** Commitment needs a normalization frontend that knows what is ambiguous per language. Do we build a minimal one covering numbers, units, and symbols for zh/en only, or is there appetite for a shared TTS text frontend that the per-model frontends eventually migrate onto?
2. **Where does segmentation live?** The `ρ` estimate is produced in Code2Wav but consumed by the text side. Does the feedback go through the connector (`construct_next_stage_streaming_input_prompt`, `distributed/omni_connectors/adapter.py:219`) or through scheduler state?
3. **Which model first?** Qwen3-TTS is the natural target since all the existing machinery is there. Should the design be validated on a second model before the interfaces are frozen?
4. **Interaction with the streaming-input scheduler state.** `num_waiting_for_streaming_input` already exists in `omni_ar_scheduler.py` and `omni_scheduler_mixin.py` for the omni thinker-to-talker path. Does a text-streamed TTS request reuse that state, or does it need a distinct one?
5. **API surface.** #1766 asks for streaming input but does not specify a wire format. Incremental text over the existing speech endpoint, or a separate streaming session? This probably deserves its own follow-up RFC and should not block the internals.
6. **Relationship to #2568.** That RFC covers concurrent streaming root causes. Confirm these do not overlap before either lands.

#### Good first issue starting points

Each of these is self-contained, useful on its own, and needs no GPU except where noted:

- **Port the ambiguity diagnostic set as a CPU-only unit test.** The paper uses 30 deliberately hard items (numbers, units, special symbols). Text in, release decision out, no model involved. This gives the commitment policy a red test to build against and is the single best entry point here.
- **Add `ρ` instrumentation to the existing ramp path.** Log realized acoustic decode steps per text token per segment in `qwen3_tts_code2wav.py`. Pure observability, no behavior change, and it produces the data the segmenter needs before the segmenter exists.
- **Add a boundary-discontinuity (PBD) helper under `vllm_omni/benchmarks/`.** Pitch, energy, and spectral jump across a seam, combined into one number. Makes mechanism 3 measurable before it is implemented.
- **Add per-concurrency first-audio-latency reporting to the TTS benchmark path.** Median and P99 over a concurrency sweep.

The three mechanisms themselves are not beginner work; they touch the scheduler, connector, and Code2Wav state. The four tasks above are, and each one de-risks a mechanism.

#### Non-goals

- Not adopting their TensorRT engine or its build pipeline.
- Not vendoring their code. The license permits it, but the code targets a different runtime; what we take is the design.
- Not a new model. Their checkpoints are not redistributed and the backbone is Qwen3-TTS, which we already support.

### Feedback Period.

Two weeks, through 2026-09-05.

Paper: X2Streaming-TTS: Causal Token-Level Text-to-Speech from Streaming Text with Speech-State Inheritance, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18661
